trust_decision.summary: Untrusted HDF5 containers must not make Keras read files outside the container: every dataset/group read out of a .keras, .weights.h5 or legacy .h5 file must pass an accessor that rejects virtual datasets, external-storage datasets and soft/external links. The decision is made at the dataset-access boundary in keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py (_verify_dataset), which at the pinned commit rejects only `dataset.external`, and it must also hold for the legacy HDF5 loader and the file editor, which bypass that boundary.

landing_point.why: It is the only dataset-storage screen in the tree and it already rejects `dataset.external`, so an engineer reading 'HDF5 virtual datasets can disclose local files' looks here and finds the `is_virtual` check missing, plus the group dereferences in H5IOStore.get just above.

fix_sites.module_kind: core saving library (H5 accessors _verify_group/_verify_dataset replaced by safe_get_h5_group/safe_get_h5_dataset)
legacy saving module (second implementation of H5 weight loading)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about .keras weight loading, while legacy_h5_format.py lives under keras/src/legacy, only serves the deprecated .h5/.hdf5 format, and performs raw `f[...]` indexing throughout, so it can be argued to be an unsupported legacy path rather than part of the reported flaw.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A missing entry path, a missing 'vars' group, or the 2.13 '_layer_checkpoint_dependencies' lookup must keep falling back to an empty group so that layers/models with no saved variables still load; a fix that raises on any missing or non-group name turns the empty-dict fallback into an exception and breaks legitimate loading (the published fix keeps an early `return self` and a `except KeyError` fallback).

O6_input_shapes: external-storage dataset (`dataset.external` non-empty) - already rejected at pinned keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py:1056
name that resolves to an h5py.SoftLink
name that resolves to an h5py.ExternalLink
entry path / 'vars' / 'model_weights' / 'optimizer_weights' / 'top_level_model_weights' that is a link instead of an in-file group
name that resolves to a Group where a Dataset is expected and vice versa
absent name or empty-dict parent (KeyError must fall back to an empty group)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: keras.saving.KerasFileEditor(path) on a .weights.h5 or .keras file: the editor walks the H5 tree with raw h5py, checks only `value.external` (file_editor.py:515) and then reads the data with `value[()]` (file_editor.py:561), so a virtual dataset or a SoftLink/ExternalLink group is read without the new guard; the read happens eagerly in __init__ (file_editor.py:100-102).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a read-only inspection/editing utility rather than a model loader, so it looks like a neighbouring feature and not the loading path the report describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package keras/src/saving, one file away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: keras.saving.load_weights('x.h5') dereferences the top-level group with raw indexing `f = f['model_weights']` (saving_api.py:312-313) before the legacy group loaders run; an ExternalLink/SoftLink at that one name is resolved by h5py and never passes safe_get_h5_group even after the published fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: h5py links are a legitimate HDF5 feature and 'model_weights' is a single convenience lookup, so it reads as a pre-existing courtesy dereference rather than part of the protected sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: adjacent file in the same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second raw-h5py weight walker with its own copy of the `external` check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the editor already duplicates the dataset-safety check instead of calling H5IOStore.__getitem__, so a maintainer touching HDF5 validation would plausibly patch one copy and leave the other.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the 2.13-compat `_layer_checkpoint_dependencies` fallback that dereferences a second attacker-controlled path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is a compat shim bolted onto H5IOStore.get, exactly the kind of lookup that gets added without routing through the shared accessor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an optimizer/EMA weight reader that returns raw h5py dataset objects
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the legacy module already returns `weights_group[weight_name]` objects instead of arrays, so a sibling reader for a new weight kind would naturally skip any guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a direct `f[name]` group dereference at a public API boundary
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: saving_api already opens h5py directly and hand-resolves 'model_weights', so another hand-resolved group name is easy to add.

O9_family: CWE-73 external control of file name/path: reading local files through HDF5 virtual datasets, external storage and links

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e . (numpy, h5py, ml_dtypes, rich, absl-py plus one backend: tensorflow/jax/torch); pytest
O10_build.project_tests: keras/src/saving/saving_lib_test.py (SavingH5IOStoreTest at line 1149), keras/src/saving/file_editor_test.py, keras/src/legacy/saving/legacy_h5_format_test.py; no test at the pinned commit mentions external/is_virtual/SoftLink/ExternalLink datasets in keras/src/saving

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if dataset.is_virtual: raise ValueError(...)` to H5IOStore._verify_dataset (keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py:1051) and stop, leaving the legacy .h5 loaders and KerasFileEditor on raw h5py indexing.

out_of_scope_notes: The bundled patch-release diff (fix.diff:5-1324) also contains unrelated fixes: keras/src/utils/file_utils.py archive-extraction hardening, keras/src/models/functional.py loop/missing-node errors, keras/src/export/openvino.py import, keras/src/version.py bump, and an h5py LazyModule; only the safe_get_h5_group/safe_get_h5_dataset hunks belong to this advisory and only those are counted as fix sites.

The pinned tree already contains several of those unrelated fixes and their tests (keras/src/models/functional.py:613-648, keras/src/models/functional_test.py:903), and keras/src/utils/module_utils.py:66 already defines `h5py = LazyModule("h5py")`, so fix.diff's base is the 3.12.1 release branch rather than the pinned master commit; the HDF5 virtual-dataset flaw itself is still open at the pinned commit (no `is_virtual` anywhere in keras/src).
